into features.csv but deliberately outside the model contract, each with a reason
code. tgp_delta_7d is in it, tagged held-out-pending-graduation.

detector that skipped whatever the lock contains cannot detect a column wrongly IN

"tgp_delta_7d" entry from NON_MODEL_COLUMNS.

     LOCKED_FEATURE_COLUMNS — note ORDER: APPEND, never insert or sort; a

fps-3jj.19.author: Edwin Steele
fps-3jj.19.text:
ORDERING CORRECTION (fps-3jj.14, 2026-08-23) — this bead's "freeze, then generate" order
is now incomplete, and following it as written costs batch2 an extra ~2h run discovered
late.

`batch_freeze.freeze_batch` computes the noise floor as its final step by calling
`compute_noise_floor(batch_dir, tank=tank)` — arity defaults to 1. So a freshly frozen
batch ALWAYS has a 1-column floor. Since fps-3jj.14 landed, `dossier_tables._noise_band`
refuses to grade a k-column candidate against a floor with fewer columns, so every
multi-column candidate in batch2 would be refused by the floor its own freeze produced.

At batch2's size (10-15 candidates) that is not a corner case: on batch1's evidence most
candidates are 2-3 column groups.

Sequence that actually works, and the one fps-3jj.14's own bead body specifies
("Generation happens FIRST — the calibration should be sized to the column counts the
batch actually contains rather than a guess"):

  1. Freeze batch2. Accept the arity-1 floor it produces; it is still the right ruler for
     any 1-column candidate and costs nothing extra.
  2. Run the generator. RECORD EVERY CANDIDATE'S COLUMN COUNT (already a filing
     obligation in generator.md § Filing).
  3. THEN one more floor run at the batch's MODAL (or max) arity, before any candidate is
     dossiered:
       noise_floor batch2 --arity <k> --n-draws <floor(30/k)> --out-name noise_floor_k<k>.json
     Note the draw pools bind on n_draws * arity against a 30-seed pool, so max draws is
     floor(30/k) — 10 at k=3, 7 at k=4.
  4. Decide which file is batch2's ruler (see below) BEFORE re-enabling the launch routine.

Known rough edge to expect at step 4: `_noise_band` reads the hardcoded filename
`noise_floor.json`, so "make the k=3 floor this batch's ruler" is a manual rename
(`noise_floor.json` -> `noise_floor_k1.json`, then `noise_floor_k<k>.json` ->
`noise_floor.json`). Reversible and it preserves both, but there is no supported
"which floor is the ruler" selector. If batch2 makes that annoying enough, that is the
change to ask for rather than working around it each time.

fps-3jj.5.author: Edwin Steele
fps-3jj.5.text:
[fps-3jj.6] The dossier routine (PR #301) is built against two assumptions about this issue's implementation — flagging so they don't silently diverge:

1. **claim.json contract.** Stale-claim recovery in `experiments/pipeline/dossier_tables.py` (`find_stale_claims`) expects the launch routine to write `<run_dir>/claim.json = {"bead_id": ..., "candidate": ..., "started_at": <ISO8601 UTC>}` the moment it claims a candidate bead, before launching the runner detached. If the launch routine doesn't produce this file, stale claims (crashed launches) become invisible to the dossier routine and never get released back to `bd ready`.
2. **Run-directory layout.** dossier_tables.py assumes one subdirectory per candidate under `experiments/candidates/<batch>/<candidate-name>/` (results.json/rowpreds.parquet/fills.parquet/run.log all together) — i.e. the launch routine must override `run_candidate(..., out_dir=...)` rather than relying on its default (`candidate_path.parent`, which would collide across candidates sharing a batch dir).

Both are documented in `docs/routines/dossier.md` ("Known gaps to flag, not silently work around"). If fps-3jj.5 ends up doing something different, please update that doc (not just the code) so the two routines stay in sync — same rationale as the shim-vs-scheduler decision (fps-6zj).

fps-3jj.9.author: Edwin Steele
fps-3jj.9.text:

Empirical handle from the fps-nor rerun (experiments/candidates/batch0/tgp_delta_7d/diagnostic_baseline_composition.py, same frozen batch0 snapshot, 14 folds, seed 42, correct 54-col baseline):

- pooled delta_cpl_held = +0.0059 c/L
- per-fold pooled contributions span -0.209 to +0.654 c/L, i.e. the largest single fold is ~110x the pooled result and they nearly cancel
- the two arms differ on 11 of 752 fills each way (1.5%); the two BASELINES, which differ by 10 whole feature columns, differ on 6/7 fills
- fold 10: 1 differing fill -> -0.046 c/L pooled. So one buy/wait flip is worth ~0.05 c/L pooled.

That last figure is the punchline: the -0.039 c/L that GRADUATED tgp_delta_7d in June is smaller than one decision flip. -0.039 (June), +0.0059 (correct baseline, now) and +0.0941 (wrong baseline) are all within a couple of flips of zero and of each other.

fps-490.author: Edwin Steele
fps-490.text:
Blocked on fps-ajs (2026-09-05, from fps-nas).

This issue grades each locked block pass/fail against
`experiments/batches/batch1/noise_floor.json`, and that file is about to be replaced. fps-nas
decided (criterion 5) to grade candidates on a broad 410-station population rather than the
five commute stations; fps-916 stamps the population into the floor and refuses a
cross-population grade, then fps-ajs recomputes the floor at 410.

Why this blocks rather than merely cautions: the bar this issue exists to validate is stated
in band-sd units (alpha ~= 0.10, 1.451 band-sd = 0.145 c/L @ 1d), and the band sd is exactly
what changes. Measured on batch1/tgp_cycle_displacement, grading a broad-population delta
against the extant FIVE-station band flips it from clears (z -2.330) to fails (z -1.544). Block

fps-ghr.author: Edwin Steele
fps-ghr.text:
ROOT CAUSE of the coverage holes — mechanical, and mostly a PIPELINE AMPLIFICATION
rather than raw data absence.

Two stages compound:

1. fuel_signal/fill.py: MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS = 28. Gaps where
   (entry_date - last_date).days <= 28 are forward-filled; anything longer is left
   unfilled entirely, deliberately ("station likely closed or rebuilt"). So the
   smallest raw gap that survives into the frame is 28 missing days.

2. fuel_signal/labels.py: a label needs 90 contiguous lookback days AND 7 contiguous
   forward days (rolling(lookback_days, min_periods=lookback_days), plus the explicit
   "window does not span exactly N calendar days" checks at lines 151/162). Around any
   surviving hole that strips a further 7 rows before and 90 rows after.

Predicted minimum hole in the modelling frame: 28 + 7 + 90 = 125 days.
OBSERVED minimum across all 245 holes: exactly 125 days. Median 132 -> implies a
~35-day raw outage. Zero holes shorter than 125 exist, which is the signature of this
mechanism rather than of independent station closures.

Consequence worth stating plainly: a station that stops reporting for one month
disappears from the model for four and a half.

The Feb-2022 cohort: hole starts cluster 2022-02-16/21/22/23, returns cluster
2022-06-28/29/30 (52 stations). Working back through the two stages, the underlying
raw outage is roughly late Feb -> late March 2022 for ~52 Sydney stations
simultaneously.

HYPOTHESIS, NOT VERIFIED: that window coincides with the Feb-March 2022 eastern
Australia floods (Sydney flooding in early March 2022). Cheap test: are the ~52
affected stations geographically clustered? Station metadata (suburb/postcode/LGA)
is needed for this and was not readily available from the experiment artifacts —
the cleaned CSVs carry Suburb/Postcode but no station_code.

This reframes the bead: the question is no longer only "does panel composition
contaminate network aggregates" but also "is a 125-day minimum exclusion the right
policy". Two sub-questions:
  - Is MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS = 28 plus a 90-day label lookback jointly too aggressive?
    A shorter re-qualification path (e.g. allow labels once 90 days of POST-return
    data exist, which is what already happens, but reconsider whether the 28-day
    fill cliff should instead taper) would return stations sooner.
  - Does the synchronised 575 -> 642 panel jump move the locked network aggregates?
    That test is unchanged and still the decisive one.

fps-ghr.author: Edwin Steele
fps-ghr.text:
DECISIVE TEST RUN (2026-08-25). Verdict: composition drift is REAL but BOUNDED and
concentrated in a handful of days. Low priority, cheap fix available.

Method: chain-linked index. Each day's change in the network mean is measured only
over stations present on BOTH that day and the previous day, then cumulated. Any
divergence from the naive full-panel mean is composition drift by construction. Run
over 2021-11-05..2025-04-17, 1260 dates x 714 stations, from data/features.parquet.

(A first attempt compared a "balanced panel" of the 348 always-present stations
against the full panel. That test was too weak to conclude from: those 348 are not a
representative subsample, so the two means differ by ~1 c/L sd continuously, which
swamps any artifact below that size. The chain-linked design has no such problem.)

RESULTS
  total composition drift over the 3.4y window : +0.461 c/L
  drift range                                  : -1.181 .. +0.568 c/L
  daily |drift change|: median 0.0000, p99 0.0959, max 0.5669 (on 2022-06-29)

The median daily drift change is EXACTLY ZERO -- on most days the panel does not
change and the artifact is nil. It is concentrated in ~8 days across 3.4 years:

  2022-06-29  +0.567 c/L  (panel +32 stations)
  2022-02-07  +0.256      (+13)
  2022-06-28  +0.206      (+19)
  2022-02-17  -0.149      (-11)
  2024-03-01  +0.138       (-3)
  2022-01-06  -0.130       (+5)
  2024-01-29  +0.116       (-3)
  2021-12-08  -0.114       (+2)

Across the Feb-2022-cohort return week (2022-06-27 -> 07-05) the drift accumulates
+0.876 c/L.

WHY IT MATTERS DESPITE BEING SMALL: the network mean feeds
station_minus_sydney_avg_cents directly, and lga_mean_cents / brand_mean_cents feed
their own station_minus_* derivatives. So on those ~8 days every station's
relative-price features are biased by up to ~0.6 c/L for bookkeeping reasons. For
scale, the project's live headroom is 2.97 c/L and no single feature has ever
delivered 0.5 c/L alone -- so the artifact is not negligible on the days it occurs,
even though it touches few rows.

ALSO FOUND: the count of LGAs with a computed lga_mean_cents steps 28 -> 30 exactly
at 2022-06-28, as two LGAs cross the ">= 3 non-Sticky stations" floor. So composition
change alters feature AVAILABILITY, not just level. network_px_std never goes NaN
(the Competitive cohort never drops below 2).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT -- what this test did NOT cover. It measured a plain mean over all
stations present. Production uses a Competitive-cohort sample std (network_px_std)
and non-Sticky, >=3-station LGA/brand means. Those cohorts churn for a SECOND reason
this test cannot see: a station's station_class can change from one snapshot_date to
the next, moving it in or out of the cohort with no data-availability change at all.
That churn could be larger than the availability churn measured here. Testing it
needs the station_class table, which is not populated in this checkout
(data/fuel.sqlite is 0 bytes). This is the remaining open question on this bead.

SUGGESTED FIX (cheap, if pursued): chain-link the aggregates, or compute the level
on a fixed cohort and apply changes only over stations present in consecutive
snapshots. Either removes the artifact by construction.

fps-ghr.author: Edwin Steele
fps-ghr.text:
COHORT CHARACTERISATION + ROOT-CAUSE UPDATE (2026-08-25). The Feb-2022 disappearance
is NOT a real-world outage and NOT a rename. The raw data is continuous; the gap is
manufactured somewhere between data/cleaned/*.csv and the modelling frame.

Method: recovered station metadata from data/snapshots/**/*.csv (station_code + name/
address/suburb/brand; 3,295 stations), matched to data/cleaned/*.csv on a normalised
address key (703 of 714 panel stations matched, 1,098,701 raw rows).

1. GEOGRAPHY -- scattered, not a flood footprint. The 52 are spread right across
   Sydney: Dural, Heathcote, Randwick, Moorebank, Cremorne, Woollahra, Concord,
   Five Dock, Kingsford, Kensington. Postcode 20xx is over-represented (53.8% of
   cohort vs 19.1% of panel) but that is inner/eastern/southern Sydney generally, not
   a contiguous affected area. The Feb-March 2022 flood hypothesis is NOT supported.

2. BRAND -- skewed, but the skew does not explain anything. On 2026 labels the cohort
   is 28.8% Ampol Foodary and 28.8% BP against panel shares of 11.2% and 15.5%. In the
   2022 raw feed they were mostly Coles Express, BP and 7-Eleven.

3. MASS RENAME -- REFUTED, and refuted in the opposite direction. Comparing each
   station's brand before 2022-02-24 with its brand after 2022-03-25:
     cohort  brand changed   1 / 51 =  2.0%
     control brand changed  68 / 604 = 11.3%
   The cohort was five times LESS likely to rebrand than the rest of the panel. The
   dominant transition of that period (EG Ampol -> Caltex Woolworths, 59 stations)
   sits almost entirely in the CONTROL group. Whatever removed the cohort from the
   frame, it was not a name or brand change.
   (An earlier pass of this check reported 15/51 brand+name changes. That was wrong --
   it used groupby().last()/.first() on an unsorted frame, so "pre" and "post" were
   arbitrary rows rather than the chronological boundary values. Corrected above.)

4. THE ACTUAL FINDING -- the raw feed never went quiet. Distinct cohort stations
   reporting E10 per month, Nov 2021 -> Sep 2022:
     cohort (of 52):  50 50 51 50 49 51 50 51 50 49 47
     control (of 651): 537 539 587 586 566 584 584 579 574 572 580
   Feb 2022 = 50, March 2022 = 49. No dip whatsoever. Same for U91/P95/P98/DL, so it
   is not a fuel-grade switch either. 51 of 52 cohort stations have raw rows inside
   the 2022-02-24..2022-03-30 window.

   So data/cleaned/*.csv HAS continuous E10 prices for these stations across a window
   in which the modelling frame shows nothing. The loss is introduced downstream --
   in the cleaned-CSV -> daily_prices ingestion (fuel_signal.db) or in whatever DB
   state features.parquet was built from.

   LEADING HYPOTHESIS, NOT CONFIRMED: the SQLite DB was populated before the
   historical CSVs were completed/backfilled and was never rebuilt from scratch.
   data/cleaned mtimes are 2026-05-02 (116 files) and 2026-05-11 (1). features.parquet
   is 2026-08-22 -- newer, but it is built FROM the DB, not from the CSVs, so its
   mtime says nothing about whether the DB ever re-read the backfilled CSVs. Cannot
   check directly here: data/fuel.sqlite and data/fuel_signal.db are both 0 bytes in
   this checkout (likely not carried through the 2026-08-18 repo move).

VERIFICATION (heavy, owner to run): rebuild from the cleaned CSVs and re-derive, then
check whether the cohort's 2022-02-24..2022-06-28 hole disappears:
    uv run python -m fuel_signal.db
    uv run python -m fuel_signal.fill
  ...then rebuild features and re-run the hole scan.
If the hole vanishes, this is a stale-DB artifact and ~198 stations x 245 holes of
"missing" history are recoverable -- which would also shrink the composition drift
measured earlier in this bead, since most of that drift is the cohort's return.

This substantially raises the value of the bead: it is no longer only "does panel
churn contaminate aggregates" but "is the model training on a frame that is missing
data we already hold on disk".

fps-ghr.author: Edwin Steele
fps-ghr.text:
ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED (2026-08-25), using experiments/batches/batch1/fuel_signal.db --
the frozen 500MB DB the batch1 runs used. No rebuild was needed.

TWO EARLIER CLAIMS IN THIS BEAD ARE WRONG. Retracting both:

  RETRACTED 1: "the raw feed never went quiet -- E10 reporting never stopped."
  That used MONTHLY buckets. Station 3 has exactly one E10 observation in March 2022
  (on the 31st), which made March look fully covered. At daily granularity the hole
  is obvious.

  RETRACTED 2: "the pipeline lost data it already has on disk", and the stale-DB /
  CSV-backfill hypothesis built on it. The DB holds exactly what the feed published.
  Nothing was lost in ingestion. There is no stale-DB bug.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

The bulk source is a price-CHANGE event log, not a daily census (README says so
explicitly). A station appears only on days it moves its price.

E10 price-change events per day across the whole panel:
  2022-02-10..03-11  100-380 stations/day   (normal)
  2022-03-12..03-20    9-51 stations/day    (collapse)
  2022-03-30           515 stations
  2022-03-31           549 stations         (mass repricing)

After the 24 Feb 2022 invasion spike, Sydney pump prices sat on a high plateau and
stations simply stopped changing them for weeks. Then on 30 March 2022 the federal
fuel excise cut (announced 29 March, ~22c/L) took effect and essentially every
station repriced on the same day -- which is why 515 and 549 stations report on
30/31 March and why the cohort all "returns" together.

So the chain is:
  1. Genuine price plateau -> station posts no E10 change for >28 days.
     e.g. station 3: last E10 observation 2022-02-23 (186.9), next 2022-03-31
     (198.9) -- a 36-day gap.
  2. fill.py MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS=28 refuses to forward-fill, treating it as
     "station likely closed or rebuilt".
  3. labels.py then strips 7 days before and 90 days after.
  4. Net: a 125+ day hole in the modelling frame.

Confirmed panel-wide: 81 stations have a >28d E10 gap starting Feb-Apr 2022, and
ALL 25 sampled cohort stations do (0 exceptions).

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL BEAD

The data is correct and the ingestion is correct. The defect is that fill.py's
"no price change for >28 days == closed" heuristic misfires during long price
plateaus -- and a plateau is exactly the market state where a buy/wait signal is
most valuable. The pipeline goes blind precisely when the question is hardest, and
it does so for ~12% of the panel at once.

This also fully explains the composition drift measured earlier in this bead: the
575 -> 642 jump is not stations reopening, it is the excise cut ending the plateau.

SUGGESTED DIRECTION (needs a decision, not obvious):
  - Distinguish "no price change" from "no data". The feed's own semantics make a
    long flat run a legitimate observation, not an absence. A station still listed
    in the daily snapshot but not posting a change is demonstrably open.
  - data/snapshots/ is a daily census and could serve as the liveness oracle for
    exactly this: present in snapshot + no change event == price held, fill it.
  - If MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS stays, it should at minimum not apply when other fuel
    grades at the same station are still reporting (station 3 kept posting P98/U91
    changes throughout its E10 "gap").

Recommend re-titling this bead. It is no longer about panel churn contaminating
aggregates; that turned out bounded (~0.5 c/L on ~8 days). The real finding is that
a 28-day fill cap plus a 90-day label lookback silently removes ~12% of the panel
for 4+ months whenever the market plateaus.

fps-ghr.author: Edwin Steele
fps-ghr.text:
CORRECTION (2026-08-25): it is NOT a price plateau. Retracting that from the previous
comment. It is an upstream hole in the NSW published data.

Row counts in data/raw/ (the downloaded NSW bulk CSVs, before any processing by this
project), all fuel grades, all NSW:

  10/03/2022   3581
  12/03/2022    289
  13/03/2022    163
  16/03/2022     95
  20/03/2022     49     <- ~98% below normal
  25/03/2022    727
  29/03/2022    691
  30/03/2022   2836
  01/04/2022   8882

data/cleaned/ mirrors this exactly, so the thinning is NOT introduced by this
project's download, clean or ingest steps. The NSW bulk feed for roughly 12-24 March
2022 is simply incomplete.

Corroborating signature in the DB: P95 and P98 sit at literally ZERO events statewide
from 2022-03-11 to 2022-03-29 while E10/U91 continue at reduced volume. Zero premium
price changes across NSW for 19 days is not physically possible, so this is missing
data rather than an unusually quiet market. The network E10 median also moved
183.9 -> 176.9 -> 185.8 -> 198.9 across the window that station 3 supposedly held one
price, which independently rules out the plateau reading.

(Also retracting the earlier suggestion that data/snapshots/ could act as a liveness
oracle here. Snapshots only start 2026-08 -- there is no 2022 coverage. Owner flagged
this; it was a bad suggestion.)

PROVENANCE of the cap: commit 87bd867, 2026-05-11,
"feat: cap forward-fill gap length to exclude closed-station periods (closes #30)".
Rationale in the message: "preventing stale prices from polluting label computation
and cycle detection during station closures/rebuilds". So the constant was chosen
deliberately for CLOSURES. A source-side publication outage was not a case it was
designed against, and it cannot distinguish the two -- both present as one long gap.

PROPOSED FIX (uses the signature that actually separates the two cases):
A genuine closure is IDIOSYNCRATIC -- one station goes dark while the rest of the
panel reports normally. A feed outage is SYNCHRONISED -- a large fraction of the
panel has a gap spanning the same dates. So gate the cap on concurrency:

  - For a candidate gap on station S spanning [a,b], measure what fraction of the
    panel also has no observation across [a,b].
  - If that fraction is high (feed outage), forward-fill through it regardless of
    length -- the station was demonstrably trading, we just were not told the price.
  - If it is low (real closure), keep the current 28-day refusal.

This is strictly better than tuning MAX_GAP_FILL_DAYS, which cannot separate the
cases at any threshold. It would recover ~81 stations x 4+ months for March 2022
alone, and would generalise to any future feed interruption.

Caveat worth stating: filling through a 19-day publication hole means carrying a
stale price across a window in which the market moved ~15-20 c/L. That is its own
distortion and arguably worse than exclusion for LABEL purposes. A reasonable
compromise is to fill for panel-membership/aggregate purposes (so the station keeps
contributing to network_px_std, lga_mean_cents etc. and does not vanish for 4 months)
while leaving LABELS unlabelled across the affected span. Needs a decision.

`experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/` on that branch:
- `README.md` — the plan, the sampling scheme's justification, and the comparison contract
- `timing.py` — criterion 1. Times `fit` / `load_history` / `replay` SEPARATELY at 5/50/200

- `homogeneity.py` — criteria 3-4. One candidate (`tgp_cycle_displacement`) at both

**Findings already in hand, before any run:**
1. **607 of 751 stations are eligible across 32 councils** over batch1's real 14-fold span
   (2021-11-06..2024-12-29). A ~120x wider universe is available if it is affordable.
2. **The reference five are not homogeneous on coverage.** Station 414 (BP Valley Heights)

3. **`aggregate_backtest` silently skips a station with no data in a window** and

4. **Reason to doubt the bead's structural costing:** `ModelStrategy.decide` calls
   `predict_proba` on ONE row per station-day. At the locked 1d cadence a 200-station,

5. **`fps-enx` filed:** `r0_cache.joblib` is keyed only on `batch_dir`, so alternating

fps-nas.text:
## Finding that changes the bead's premise (2026-09-05, from PR #361 review)

**The incumbent five-station arbiter is a FOUR-station instrument across two of its
fourteen folds.** Station 414 (BP Valley Heights) has this per-fold E10 coverage
vector over batch1's real 14-fold geometry (2021-11-05 .. 2025-04-17):

    [0.96, 1.00, 1.00, 0.33, 0.00, 0.00, 0.10, 1.00 x7]

Folds 5 and 6 are ENTIRELY dark; folds 4 and 7 are barely covered. Four of fourteen
folds unusable. `aggregate_backtest` silently skips a station whose window CPL is
NaN, so this has never announced itself — and the span-level figure (0.742) makes it
look merely thin rather than absent. The other four preferred stations are clean
(1.00 across every fold, bar two 0.96s).

Why this matters for fps-nas beyond data hygiene:

1. **The "~92 independent decisions" figure is optimistic.** Those decisions are not
   evenly spread across 5 stations x 14 folds; two folds have 20% less population
   than assumed and two more are close to it.
2. **It sharpens the homogeneity caveat.** The reference population is not
   homogeneous on coverage *with itself* across time, so a broad-vs-five comparison
   differs on an axis unrelated to any candidate feature. Report both populations'
   coverage; do not filter the five (they are exogenous — the owner's actual commute).
3. **It is an argument FOR widening**, independent of the resolution argument the
   bead already makes.

Second measurement, a limitation rather than a defect: `fill.py` forward-fills gaps
of <= 28 days into `daily_prices`, so a presence count sees only >28-day darkness and
everything shorter is a stale price the replay trades on as live (up to 27 consecutive
days). **Two-thirds of every day the arbiter has ever replayed is forward-filled** —
median 0.663 at the five, 0.679 across the 599-station eligible pool. Pre-existing and
unchanged by any of this work. Medians differ by 1.02x so composition does not bite
there, but the tail does: 64.8% of the broad pool carries a >= 21-day filled run
against 40% of the five. `describe_universe` now reports `observed_fraction_*` for
both populations so a homogeneity read can see it rather than assume it.

Both measured independently and reproduced by a second session; neither is a claim
about a candidate feature, so neither is blocked on the timing/homogeneity runs.

fps-nas.text:
## Addendum: 414's dark folds DO intersect the shock set (2026-09-05)

Cheap check suggested by the PR #361 reviewer, and it comes back positive.

414's degraded folds are {4, 5, 6, 7} (coverage 0.33 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.10).
batch1's empirical shock set (`experiments/batches/batch1/shock_folds.json`,
corrected set per fps-hnp) is **{1, 3, 4, 14}**.

**Fold 4 is in both.** And it is not an incidental fold: `fold_baseline_ll` puts it at
**0.4218**, the second-hardest of the fourteen (only fold 1 at 0.4254 is worse). So the
arbiter evaluates one of its two hardest folds — and a shock fold, which several
candidate signatures are graded on — with 414 contributing about a third of its days.
Folds 5 and 6 (414 fully dark, four-station instrument) are NOT in the shock set, and
fold 7 (0.10) is not either.

Why this is worth carrying into the write-up rather than filing as data hygiene:

- The per-fold noise band is not constant across folds, and nothing currently records
  that it varies. A fold-level regression read as signal is being read against a band
  that is wider in folds 4-7 than elsewhere, for a reason unrelated to any feature.
- It lands specifically on the regime axis. `TARGET`/zone grading (fps-3jj) splits
  shock vs normal, so the one contaminated fold sits in the smaller of the two cells
  (4 shock folds vs 10 normal), where it carries proportionally more weight.
- Bounded, not fatal: one of four shock folds is affected, and only partially (0.33,
  not 0.00). This is a caveat to state when reading a zone verdict, not a reason to
  discard one.

Does NOT change the recommendation to widen; if anything it strengthens the third
bullet of the previous comment — the argument for widening that does not depend on the
resolution argument, and therefore survives even if the timing run says a broad
universe is impractical.

## Correction to my 414 comments above (2026-09-05, post-merge)

Two of my earlier claims need narrowing. Checked against
`project_preferred_station_outages`, which already documented most of this.

**1. The four-fold hole was NOT a new finding.** That memory already records "folds 4-7:
414 genuinely closed (rebuild) — an honest 4-station market", and fold 1 as a
**3-station SHOCK fold** (414 and 18517 both dark). My per-fold vector corroborates it
from a different table, nothing more. And fold 1 is the worse case, not fold 4: 3
stations on a shock fold beats 414-at-0.33 on one.

**2. The shock intersection is real but I named the wrong fold as the headline.**
Shock set is {1, 3, 4, 14}. Fold 1 (3-station) and fold 4 (414 at 0.33) are both in it.
Fold 1 was already known; fold 4 is the increment.

**What IS new, and it is a limitation of what just merged — bd fps-wst.**
My gate counts `daily_prices` rows. The feature frame disagrees, by construction:

| fold | station | feature rows | daily_prices |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 414 / 18517 | **0 / 0** | 86 / 86 |
| 8 | 414 | **8** | 90 |

`fill.py` forward-fills `daily_prices` for gaps <= 28d; `labels.py` strips 7d before and
90d after a gap from the feature frame. So fold 1 passes my per-window gate at 0.96
coverage while having ZERO feature rows for both Blue Mountains stations — the exact
fold the memory flags as "a measurement gap, not a thin market".

Consequence for this bead: `daily_prices` coverage is the REPLAY axis and is a valid
gate for it, but it is **not** a proxy for feature availability, so a widened universe
gated only on it can admit feature-dark stations (provider misses -> NaN; reduced
sample, silently and unevenly). Read the homogeneity result with that in mind, and
prefer fps-wst's reported-field approach over adding a second gate.

## Measurement phase COMPLETE 2026-09-05 — landed direct to main (148744b)

experiments/2026-09-05_arbiter_universe_width/ carries the full write-up, both
scripts, timing.json and homogeneity.json. INDEX.md row + ledger.yaml entry in the
same commit.

[x] 1. Timing run at 5/50/200 — **conclusion holds, both halves of the stated
       mechanism wrong.** fit 44.1s flat. Replay IS dead-linear (38.4x for 40x
       stations, ~0.058 s/station-fold) — the 18,000-predict_proba doubt raised in
       the previous handoff was physically correct, it just starts at 0.30s.
       `load_history` does NOT scale (28.3s at n=5 vs 27.4s at n=200), though the
       bead named it as one of the two scaling terms. Fixed cost is fit + history
       ~= 71s, not fit's 44s alone. Net +14% for 40x.
[x] 2. Sampling scheme — PR #361, previously recorded.
[x] 3. Broad-population CPL — run at **410**, the whole eligible pool, not the 200
       timing.py justified. Owner set the compute budget explicitly (up to 5x on
       freezes/candidate runs is cheap), which removes cost as a tiebreak; the 0.90
       coverage gate is a correctness filter not a cost one, so 410 is the ceiling
       at any budget. Measured 72 s/arm-fold at 410 vs 48 at five.
[x] 4. Homogeneity — **HOLDS.** tgp_cycle_displacement pooled delta_cpl_held:
       five -0.2077, broad(410) -0.1292. Same sign, 12/14 folds agree, r = 0.704,
       own-2*SE intervals overlap, each point estimate inside the other's interval.
[x] 5. **DECIDED: grade on the broad 410, report the five.** The broad estimate is
       both more precise (2x tighter) and less flattering, i.e. a stricter bar in
       c/L. The five stay exogenous — never filtered, sampled or gated.
[x] 6. Noise floor — addressed here, discharged by **fps-916 -> fps-ajs** (blocking
       dep set). Grading the broad delta against the EXTANT five-station band flips
       it to fail (z -1.544 vs -2.330). And the mismatch would be silent:
       `compute_noise_floor()` accepts `station_codes` (noise_floor.py:223) and
       never stamps it; `_bank_admissibility` checks baseline_fingerprint /
       tank_params / null_method / arity / partial and has no population axis. Same
       defect shape as fps-15c's cadence stamp. Costed at 410: ~3.1h at 10 draws,
       ~11h at 40.

**Three findings the bead did not ask for, all worth carrying forward:**

1. **The resolution gain is 2.00x, not 10x.** 102x the decisions (83 -> 8,476)
   halved the per-fold sd (0.7982 -> 0.3992) and no more. The fold is the
   independent replicate and widening the universe does not create folds. Sizing on
   station-days would have reported sqrt(102) ~= 10x and manufactured exactly the
   improvement under measurement — the comparison contract in the README was
   written to avoid this and it fired.
2. **Neither width clears its own fold-clustered interval** — t = 0.98 at five,
   1.27 at 410 — although both clear the placebo band the dossier grades on
   (five: z = -2.330 vs a bar of 1.923). Two rulers asking different questions: the
   band asks "could a null column produce this pooled number", the fold-clustered SE
   asks "does it repeat across folds". The project's cleanest signal passes the
   first at both widths and fails the second at both widths, and **no dossier
   currently reports the second.** Recorded as `not_decided`, not filed — whether it
   should gate anything is a design call, not a measurement.
3. **Harness validated:** the five-station arm returned -0.2077, batch1's committed
   headline to the digit, so nothing above is an artifact of homogeneity.py
   bypassing run_candidate. It must bypass it (fps-enx) — and fps-enx is now on the
   critical path, since criterion 5 means two populations coexist routinely.

**Correction landed in ledger.yaml:** fps-e6i's entry carried "PERMANENTLY
UNTESTABLE by this pipeline as configured: ... no mechanism to widen the replay
universe without changing what the arbiter is for". This run built that mechanism
and used it. Rewritten as SUPERSEDED, keeping the half that survives — the fold
count, which is what caps the gain at 2x.

Closing: all six criteria discharged, with the two follow-on beads carrying the
noise-floor work.

fps-sk0.author: Edwin Steele
fps-sk0.text:
Diagnostic notes recovered from a live run (session cse_01BGBTNYbqkvEHDEcjCvnaoE, 2026-08-14 ~05:37-05:46 UTC) that could NOT sync via bd dolt push (same bug), so its findings were trapped in that now-destroyed sandbox and only recoverable via the raw Routine session transcript. Preserving them here + a new hypothesis:

**What that run found:**
- Reproduced the 403 live, twice, with identical output each time.
- Ruled out "GitHub blanket-rejects refs/dolt/* namespace": `git ls-remote https://github.com/edwinsteele/fuel-price-signal.git 'refs/dolt/*'` succeeded and returned an existing ref, so reads to that namespace work fine.
- Checked the local egress proxy's own status endpoint (`$HTTPS_PROXY/__agentproxy/status`) for recent relay failures: 15 total, all to `gastownhall-eventsapi.com:443` (unrelated to this repo) — zero entries for github.com or any dolt-related host. If the proxy itself were blocking/rejecting the push by policy, you'd expect it to show up here.

**New hypothesis (mine, from re-reading the transcript — unverified, needs a live run to confirm):**
Pickup rule 0's fallback path (`gh auth token 2>/dev/null || echo "${GH_TOKEN:-$GITHUB_TOKEN}"`) assumes `$GH_TOKEN`/`$GITHUB_TOKEN` hold a real credential when `gh` itself is absent. In this run, `gh` genuinely wasn't installed ("gh: command not found") — this environment talks to GitHub via an MCP tool instead, not the `gh` CLI, so `gh auth token` was never going to work. The fallback then read `$GH_TOKEN`, which printed as literally `proxy-injected` (confirmed: the script's own "token present, length 14" message — `len("proxy-injected") == 14`, not a coincidence). That literal placeholder string then got embedded verbatim as the password in the Dolt remote's tokenized URL.

If `proxy-injected` is a sentinel this environment's egress proxy is meant to recognize and silently swap for a real credential (rather than a literal secret value), and if Dolt's internal git subprocess doesn't route that specific request through the proxy the way plain `git`/`gh` calls do, GitHub's real server would receive a literal, bogus `x-access-token:proxy-injected` credential and correctly reject it with 403 — which matches every symptom: `git ls-remote` (ambient, unmodified remote) works, `gh`-tool-based calls work, but the *tokenized* Dolt remote specifically fails.

This would mean fps-sk0's original framing ("egress proxy policy blocks the ref namespace") is likely wrong — the proxy isn't blocking anything; pickup rule 0 is handing Dolt a garbage credential when `gh` is unavailable.

**Proposed low-risk fix (not yet applied — needs live verification before landing):** before embedding `$GH_TOKEN`/`$GITHUB_TOKEN` into the Dolt remote URL, reject values that look like placeholders (e.g. exactly `proxy-injected`, or that don't match a real GitHub token shape like `gho_`/`ghp_`/`ghs_`/`github_pat_` prefixes) and skip the explicit remote reconfiguration in that case, falling back to whatever ambient credential handling already makes `git ls-remote` work. This can't regress the known-working case (fps-ddf's run had a real `gh`-sourced token, which would still pass the shape check).

Not landing this fix blind — it's a plausible root cause, not a confirmed one, and this issue is explicitly about not making unverified changes to shared automation. Needs one supervised live run to confirm before code changes.

fps-sk0.author: Edwin Steele
fps-sk0.text:
Root cause now conclusively narrowed by a live run (session cse_01RwJMuHfNyeBzikS8g9DoqR, 2026-08-14 07:11-07:17 UTC), after PR #292's credential-guard fix landed:

**PR #292's fix was necessary but not sufficient.** It correctly stopped embedding the bogus "proxy-injected" placeholder as a Dolt remote credential — but bd dolt push still failed with the identical 403, even with zero credential embedded (falling back purely to ambient auth).

**Decisive test:** `git push --dry-run origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>` — a real WRITE to a normal branch ref, using the exact same ambient credentials — succeeded. So this environment's ambient credentials DO support pushes in general. Only `bd dolt push`'s target (the `refs/dolt/data` custom ref namespace) is rejected with 403.

This rules out both prior hypotheses (bad/placeholder credential; blanket read-block on the namespace — reads already confirmed fine). What's left, precisely: **this environment's egress proxy or the ambient credential's underlying GitHub token is specifically blocking pushes to non-standard git ref namespaces** (`refs/dolt/*`), while permitting pushes to `refs/heads/*`. This is consistent with a common GitHub App / fine-grained-PAT restriction (broad "Contents: write" is often scoped to standard refs only, with custom namespaces requiring classic-PAT-level access).

**This is not fixable from CLAUDE.md or repo code.** It needs one of:
- A real classic PAT (full `repo` scope, not fine-grained/App-scoped) provisioned specifically for this Routine's environment for bd/dolt's push needs, or
- The environment's egress/token policy explicitly allowlisting pushes to `refs/dolt/*`, or
- A different Dolt sync transport that doesn't require a custom ref namespace.

All of these are outside what an agent session (interactive or Routine) can change — they need the owner or Anthropic support to investigate the Routine environment's (`env_013cCwqEo6PFqNSNxsYgny1k`) token provisioning/egress policy directly.

Leaving open. PR #292's guard stays merged (it's a real, if partial, improvement — no bogus credential gets embedded anymore), but the underlying push-to-custom-ref-namespace block remains.

fps-sk0.author: Edwin Steele
fps-sk0.text:
Definitive root cause confirmed via upstream research (2026-08-14): this is dolthub/dolt#10486 — https://github.com/dolthub/dolt/issues/10486 — an open, unfixed bug filed by Dolt's own team: "Currently git credentials that require an inline password do not work with dolt push, pull, fetch. These commands make a lot of changes to stdin, stdout, and stderr which is preventing this from getting to the git command." Zero comments, no fix shipped as of this writing.

This environment's ambient git auth uses an interactive-style mechanism (GIT_ASKPASS) — fine for plain `git push`/`git ls-remote` (both confirmed working), fatal for Dolt's own push/pull because of the linked bug. Two fix attempts landed in CLAUDE.md (PR #292: reject placeholder tokens before embedding; PR #4319652 direct-to-main: install `gh` if missing so a real token can be embedded, sidestepping Dolt's askpass bug entirely) — both correct in principle, but a live run (2026-08-14 07:29 UTC) proved this specific sandbox has no path to a real token at all: `curl` to `api.github.com` returns 403, downloading a GitHub release tarball returns 404 — this environment routes ALL GitHub API/file access through an internal MCP tool, not raw HTTPS, so `gh` cannot even be installed here to produce a real token.

Net position: not fixable from CLAUDE.md or repo code. Two independent blockers stacked:
1. Dolt's own upstream bug (dolthub/dolt#10486) — needs a Dolt fix, or a token embedded directly in the URL as a workaround.
2. This sandbox provides no mechanism to obtain a real, embeddable token (no working `gh`, no installable `gh`, proxy-sentinel env vars only) — needs an Anthropic-side change to how Claude Code Routines provisions git credentials to sandboxes (e.g. a real static token as an env var, not a proxy sentinel), OR GitHub-side confirmation of whether the Claude GitHub App's permissions (checked 2026-08-14: Code read/write, all repos — nothing obviously restrictive) actually cover non-standard ref namespaces at all.

Until one of those lands, expect every Routine run to hit this on `bd dolt push`/`pull` from a fresh checkout, and expect any writes it makes locally (issue claims, closes, comments) to be silently stuck in that run's sandbox unless reconciled by hand from a session that can push (as this comment is).

fps-sk0.author: Edwin Steele
fps-sk0.text:
External research pass (2026-08-15, interactive session): confirmed the token-embedded-URL fix already matches Dolt's own documented CI pattern (their GitHub Actions example in the announcement blog is literally `x-access-token:$TOKEN@github.com/...`), and beads' own git-integration.md has no CI-credential guidance beyond "if git is already credentialed, it works" — so this wasn't a case of missing an obvious simpler documented approach. `github.token`/GITHUB_TOKEN in .beads/config.yaml is a red herring — that's scoped to the unrelated `bd github` issue-sync integration, not Dolt remote auth. Server mode doesn't apply either — it solves same-host concurrent writers, not Mac<->ephemeral-Routine sync.

Found a concrete, more precise explanation for the "downloading a GitHub release tarball returns 404" symptom logged above. Pulled @beads/bd's actual npm postinstall.js: it downloads its own binary from `https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/releases/download/v${VERSION}/...` — the same github.com/releases/download domain the gh-install fallback targets — and that succeeds (bd installs fine in this environment). The difference: CLAUDE.md's gh-install script first hit `api.github.com/repos/cli/cli/releases/latest` to discover the version, and api.github.com is the domain already confirmed to 403 in this sandbox. An empty $GH_LATEST from that failed call would produce a malformed download URL (`.../download/v/gh__linux_amd64.tar.gz`), which predictably 404s — matching the logged symptom without requiring github.com/releases/download itself to be blocked. Revised CLAUDE.md's gh-install step to pin an exact version (2.97.0, same philosophy as the bd pin) and construct the download URL directly, removing the api.github.com dependency entirely. Not yet live-verified — needs a real Routine run to confirm gh actually installs this way.

Also found a second, independent, previously-untested failure mode while reading postinstall.js: @beads/bd's postinstall skips downloading the native binary entirely when process.env.CI is set, and bin/bd.js has no fallback download — just errors "binary not found" on first invocation. command -v bd only checks the npm shim exists, not that the binary downloaded. If this Routine's sandbox sets CI ambiently (common for container/orchestration platforms), npm install could report success while leaving bd non-functional. Added a bd --version verification step + env -u CI retry to pickup rule 0. Also not yet live-verified.

Neither of these findings changes the core diagnosis already recorded above (Dolt's askpass-class bug + no path to a real token in this sandbox) — they're refinements to the gh-install mechanics that pickup rule 0 depends on, surfaced while researching whether a "common pattern" was being missed. fps-x0f.author: Edwin Steele
fps-x0f.text:
Dependency on fps-1785999730023-4-264564ac (#265, per-zone headroom attribution)
added 2026-08-20. It binds STEP 2 specifically, not the whole issue — recording why,
since bd dependencies are issue-level and step 1 can proceed meanwhile.

Step 2 asks "does recoverable headroom concentrate in late descent", measured as
model_cpl - oracle_cpl per regime zone. That is exactly the estimator #265 exists to
fix, and #265's two defects both bite here:

VARIANCE — and this is the decisive one, discovered while wiring this dependency.
The headroom map's regime reading is late_descent 1.00 / overdue 1.33 / normal 1.50:
a total spread of 0.50 c/L. The SAME experiment calibrates its own per-band noise
floor at approximately +/-0.5 c/L (from the impossible negatives: >=16c band -0.53,
2025-01 -3.6, 2023-10 -2.9 — a perfect-foresight oracle cannot lose, so those are
attribution artifacts sizing the error). The entire regime spread therefore sits
inside the map's own error bar. "Regime axis FLAT" is more accurately "regime axis
UNRESOLVED" — it cannot distinguish 1.00 from 1.50.

That is a THIRD independent defect in the finding that rested the late-descent
thread, alongside the two already in this issue's description (the three findings
disagreeing, and the cycle_pct_through denominator). Three separate reasons to
distrust one verdict is enough to stop treating it as settled. #265's
station-bootstrap CIs are precisely what settles it: a cell reporting 1.00 +/- CI
either clears 1.50 or does not.

BIAS — path coupling is expected to be WORSE on a phase axis than on the volatility
axis #265 was written against. #265's mechanism is that the oracle buys cheaply just
before an expensive zone and coasts through it, so the saving lands in the
neighbouring zone. Cycle-phase zones are by construction temporally adjacent and
cyclic, and the oracle's optimal play IS to buy at trough and coast through peak and
early descent. So the saving generated by correctly timing a late-descent trough
entry is structurally likely to be attributed to a neighbouring phase zone. A
per-phase-zone headroom number is close to the worst case for this artifact.

Consequence for sequencing: do not run step 2 on the current estimator. Doing so
would repeat the failure this issue exists to correct — reaching a verdict on an
instrument that cannot support it. Step 1 (fix or bound the phase axis) does not
touch per-zone headroom and can proceed in parallel; step 3 uses the log-loss screen
and the realised arbiter, not this estimator.

Worth noting the two fixes compose rather than conflict: #265 fixes HOW headroom is
attributed within a zone, step 1 fixes WHICH ROWS are in the zone. Both are wrong
today and they are independent errors.

fps-x0f.author: Edwin Steele
fps-x0f.text: Step 2 blocked measure identified 2026-08-20 (fps-...-264564ac, commit b6e0a9c): per-zone headroom CANNOT answer 'is late descent a real target', at any sample size. Not a noise problem - the decomposition depends on free bookkeeping conventions that move each zone further than the zones differ. Every per-zone row of #262 is withdrawn, including the 'regime axis FLAT' finding that rested this thread; #262's window-level 1.66 c/L stands. Replacement under consideration: decision-timing accuracy (did the model pick a worse week than the oracle?) - a rate, not a cost, so nothing is allocated to a period and all three conventions vanish. Also lower variance: ~124 late-descent decisions give +/-4.5pp on a rate vs +/-0.7 c/L on the cost.

fps-x0f.author: Edwin Steele
fps-x0f.text:
fps-grp (PR #319, 2026-08-21) collapses this bead's three-way contradiction. Of the three
mutually-inconsistent late-descent findings, THE TWO THAT DISAGREED WITH EACH OTHER are now
both withdrawn:

  1. Gate-1 Layer-1 proxy regret (1.05 / 1.72 / 1.32)  -> late descent WORST   -> STANDS
  2. Gate-1 Layer-2 realised saving% (0.64/2.13/4.06%) -> late descent BETTER  -> WITHDRAWN (fps-grp)
  3. #262 per-regime headroom (1.50 / 1.00 / 1.33)     -> late descent LEAST   -> WITHDRAWN 2026-08-20

Row 2 goes for the same reason row 3 did: realised CPL is a path-coupled total, and tagging a
fill by the regime at its own date allocates it to a sub-period, which has no unique answer.
Demonstrated on committed numbers, no re-run -- emergency-fill inclusion is a free convention
(Layer 2 includes forced fills, Layer 3 excludes them; both defensible) worth 21.30 / 8.15 /
13.69 c/L per bucket against a between-bucket spread of 6.73-10.40, and it REVERSES the
ordering. Note this takes Layer 3 with it: the flat chosen-only CPL 174.5/176.4/176.4 -- sorry,
174.5/176.4/174.9 -- is a second draw from the same unidentified quantity, not the corrected
version of Layer 2. Row 1 survives because expected_cents_per_row is a per-row TP/FP/FN
classification score: no tank, no ledger, no path.

What this changes here:

- **Step 1 is re-scoped, not blocked.** It is no longer "why do three findings disagree" --
  there is nothing left to reconcile. It is: one surviving reading, it is a PROXY not the
  arbiter, its tau is re-picked inside each bucket, and it is cut on the known-defective
  expanding-mean cycle_mean_length axis. The axis defect (this bead's actual step 1) is
  untouched by fps-grp and still needs fixing or bounding.
- **The realised regime axis has never been measured with an identified instrument, in either
  direction.** So "is late descent a target?" is genuinely OPEN, not leaning either way.
- **The thread was RESTED on row 3**, which is withdrawn -- so that closure argument is gone
  independently of whether its conclusion was right. Don't re-cite it.
- **Step 2's redirect is unchanged and now load-bearing:** it needs a measure that never
  allocates cost to a period. Candidates that pass the fps-grp test: decision-timing accuracy
  vs the oracle ("did the model pick a worse week?"), buy/wait agreement rates, per-row
  log-loss -- all natively stamped at a moment. Or express the zone as a set of FOLDS, since
  each (fold, station) is an independent simulation with its own tank and a fold-cut number
  allocates nothing.

Full enumeration and the arithmetic: experiments/2026-08-21_path_coupling_audit/README.md.

fps-zci.author: Edwin Steele
fps-zci.text:
ORDER IS PART OF THE CONTRACT TOO (found 2026-08-19, batch0 calibration re-run).

The corrected 54-column batch0 run returned +0.0439, not the +0.0059 my hand-run reference gave. Same 54 columns, same seed 42, same snapshot — and the BASELINE arm differed too, so it is nothing to do with the candidate.

Cause: column ORDER. baseline_columns.json is sorted alphabetically; every June experiment, the TEMPLATE, and train_lgbm all use group order (FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS + NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS). Verified directly: same 54 columns at seed 42, sorted vs grouped, gives 732/47823 val rows different probabilities (max |dp| = 0.090, mean 4.7e-4). LightGBM breaks equal-gain split ties by feature index, and with 35 near-identical LGA trough columns exact ties are common. Realised effect: 0.038 c/L on the pooled delta — about 0.8 of a decision flip.

THE PART THAT MATTERS MOST: the locked artifact is GROUP ORDER.
  joblib.load('data/models/lgbm_calibrated.joblib')['feature_columns'] == FEATURE_COLUMNS + LGA_FEATURE_COLUMNS + NETWORK_FEATURE_COLUMNS  -> True
  ... == sorted(same)  -> False
  52 of 54 column indices differ between the two orders.
So even after fps-sa1 fixed the column SET, the pipeline's R0 is still not the production model. Same bug class, one level down.

resolve_baseline_columns()'s sorted() has a stated motive — 'Sorted so the on-disk contract is stable regardless of column insertion order' — which is exactly backwards. Sorting makes the FILE diff-stable while making the MODEL unstable to feature additions: inserting one alphabetically-early column reshuffles every index after it, perturbing the model everywhere and breaking comparability with every prior run. Group/append order leaves existing indices untouched when a new group is appended.

Implications for this issue's shape:
1. Drop sorted() from resolve_baseline_columns(); canonical order = production order = group order.
2. Item 3's artifact check must be an ORDERED comparison (==, not set equality).
3. Item 5's fingerprint must hash the ORDERED list, not the set.
4. New: column order is an undeclared SECOND SEED. The project has seed discipline (multi-seed when delta logloss <~ 3x seed std) but nobody varies or reports order, so every cross-run comparison carries an unmeasured order term. Worth measuring order-variance against seed-variance once, so we know whether it needs the same discipline.

Checked and clean: no feature-column list anywhere is built from unordered set iteration (every set() use in fuel_signal/ and experiments/ is a membership test or immediately sorted()). That would have been worse — Python string hashing is randomised per process, so it would be non-reproducible run to run.

fps-zci.author: Edwin Steele
fps-zci.text:
MEASURED: order-variance is ~2% of seed-variance. Pin it; do NOT give it multi-seed discipline.

One train/val slice (2019-11-05..2021-11-05 train, 430,283 rows; 2021-11-05..2022-02-03 val, 47,823 rows), 5 draws each arm. SEED arm = group order fixed, seed over SEEDS. ORDER arm = seed 42 fixed, order over group/sorted/3 random permutations.

                logloss std   logloss range   n_buy std   n_buy range
  ORDER            0.000258        0.000630        11.7            29
  SEED             0.015643        0.041815       497.0          1136
  ORDER/SEED           0.02x                          0.02x

Decision flips at tau=0.25 vs the arm's first draw:
  ORDER: 8 / 14 / 29 / 8 rows   (0.017% - 0.061%)
  SEED : 1743 / 2069 / 1768 / 1892 rows   (3.6% - 4.3%)

So item 4 of this issue resolves NEGATIVE: column order does not need the multi-seed treatment the project applies to seeds. It is a ~100x smaller perturbation. Pinning the canonical order (production group order) is sufficient, and is worth doing anyway for determinism and for parity with the locked artifact.

THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING, though: that same 0.02%-of-decisions perturbation moved the pooled realised delta_cpl_held by 0.038 c/L -- about 0.8 of a decision flip -- on the batch0 tgp_delta_7d run (group order +0.0059, sorted +0.0439, otherwise identical). A change far too small to matter for model quality is large enough to reorder the arbiter's headline. That is not a fact about column order; it is another measurement of the arbiter differencing two nearly-identical quantities, i.e. the same thing fps-3jj.9 exists to characterise, reached from a different direction.

Also confirmed by the same work: the pipeline itself is exact. An independently written script in the pipeline's column order reproduced its run to 7 decimal places (R0 189.6959584, cand 189.7398851, both diff 0.0000000), and the .asof vs exact-key provider difference (822 hits / 88 misses) again made no difference. The pipeline is trustworthy; what was not pinned is the contract handed to it.
